verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मैव सन्ततो मुक्तिर्ब्रह्मैव सन्ततो गतिः | ब्रह्मैव सन्ततो विद्या ब्रह्मैव सन्ततो मतिः ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaiva santato muktirbrahmaiva santato gatiḥ | brahmaiva santato vidyā brahmaiva santato matiḥ ||
verses.translation: Brahman alone is eternal liberation; Brahman alone is eternal path; Brahman alone is eternal knowledge; Brahman alone is eternal wisdom.
verses.hindi: ब्रह्म ही नित्य मुक्ति है; ब्रह्म ही नित्य गति है; ब्रह्म ही नित्य विद्या है; ब्रह्म ही नित्य मति है।
verses.commentary: The affirmation that Brahman is the source and goal of all spiritual pursuits. Liberation, path, knowledge, and wisdom are all expressions of the same reality.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation that Brahman is the source and goal of all spiritual pursuits. Liberation, path, knowledge, and wisdom are all expressions of the same reality.

verses.sanskrit: काशी क्षेत्रं शरीरं त्रिभुवनजननी व्यापिनी ज्ञानगङ्गा | भक्तिः शर्वो गुरुः स्यान्मुक्तिरेव च काशी ||
verses.transliteration: kāśī kṣetraṃ śarīraṃ tribhuvanajananī vyāpinī jñānagaṅgā | bhaktiḥ śarvo guruḥ syānmuktireva ca kāśī ||
verses.translation: The body itself is the sacred field of Kashi; wisdom is the all-pervading Ganga, mother of three worlds; devotion is Shiva; the guru is liberation — this itself is Kashi.
verses.hindi: शरीर ही काशी क्षेत्र है; ज्ञानगंगा त्रिभुवन की जननी, व्यापिनी है; भक्ति ही शिव है; गुरु ही मुक्ति है — यही काशी है।
verses.commentary: The Jabala's most celebrated verse: Kashi is not a city on the Ganga — Kashi is within you. The body is the sacred field; wisdom is the sacred river; devotion is Shiva himself; the guru is liberation itself. The external pilgrimage is the externalisation of an inner geography. Those who seek Kashi without knowing this may travel to Varanasi and return unchanged. Those who know this can find liberation wherever they stand.
verses.wordMeaning: The Jabala's most celebrated verse: Kashi is not a city on the Ganga — Kashi is within you. The body is the sacred field; wisdom is the sacred river; devotion is Shiva himself; the guru is liberation itself. The external pilgrimage is the externalisation of an inner geography. Those who seek Kashi without knowing this may travel to Varanasi and return unchanged. Those who know this can find liberation wherever they stand.

verses.sanskrit: यदहरेव विरजेत् तदहरेव प्रव्रजेत् | किं पाण्डित्येन किं बाल्येन ||
verses.transliteration: yadahareva virajet tadahareva pravrajet | kiṃ pāṇḍityena kiṃ bālyena ||
verses.translation: On the very day that dispassion arises, on that very day one should renounce. What is the use of scholarship? What is the use of childishness?
verses.hindi: जिस दिन वैराग्य उत्पन्न हो, उसी दिन संन्यास ले लेना चाहिए। पाण्डित्य से क्या? बाल्यभाव से क्या?
verses.commentary: One of the most radical verses in the entire Upanishadic corpus. The standard Vedic life-stages prescribe sannyasa only in old age — after brahmacharya, household life, and forest-dwelling. The Jabala overturns this: the moment of genuine vairagya (dispassion) is not predictable and not schedulable. It arises when it arises. To defer it for social convention — waiting for the "right stage" — is to betray the living moment of awakening. Equally: "what is the use of scholarship?" — scholarship that does not produce genuine dispassion is mere accumulation.
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most radical verses in the entire Upanishadic corpus. The standard Vedic life-stages prescribe sannyasa only in old age — after brahmacharya, household life, and forest-dwelling. The Jabala overturns this: the moment of genuine vairagya (dispassion) is not predictable and not schedulable. It arises when it arises. verses.sanskrit: यो ब्रह्म वेद स सर्वं वेद न ब्रह्म वेद किंचित् | यदा ब्रह्म प्रशान्ते तदा ब्रह्म प्रशान्तम् ||
verses.transliteration: yo brahma veda sa sarvaṃ veda na brahma veda kiñcit | yadā brahma praśānte tadā brahma praśāntam ||
verses.translation: He who knows Brahman knows all; he who does not know Brahman knows nothing. When Brahman is fully known, Brahman is fully at peace.
verses.hindi: जो ब्रह्म को जानता है वह सब जानता है; जो ब्रह्म को नहीं जानता वह कुछ भी नहीं जानता। जब ब्रह्म पूर्ण ज्ञात हो जाता है, तब ब्रह्म पूर्ण शांत होता है।
verses.commentary: Knowledge of Brahman is knowledge of everything, because Brahman is the substratum of all. Partial knowledge is no knowledge at all.
verses.wordMeaning: Knowledge of Brahman is knowledge of everything, because Brahman is the substratum of all. Partial knowledge is no knowledge at all.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं ब्रह्मैव सर्वं ब्रह्म मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ brahmaiva sarvaṃ brahma mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is Brahman alone, all is Brahman in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब ब्रह्म ही है, सब ब्रह्म मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Brahman; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Brahman; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: शुद्धोऽहं शुद्धोऽस्मि शुद्धोऽहं शुद्धोऽस्मि | शुद्धं ब्रह्म शुद्धं ब्रह्म शुद्धं ब्रह्म शुद्धं मम ||
verses.transliteration: śuddho'haṃ śuddho'smi śuddho'haṃ śuddho'smi | śuddhaṃ brahma śuddhaṃ brahma śuddhaṃ brahma śuddhaṃ mam ||
verses.translation: I am pure, I am pure, I am pure, I am pure; Brahman is pure, Brahman is pure, Brahman is pure, pure is mine.
verses.hindi: मैं शुद्ध हूँ, मैं शुद्ध हूँ, मैं शुद्ध हूँ, मैं शुद्ध हूँ; ब्रह्म शुद्ध है, ब्रह्म शुद्ध है, ब्रह्म शुद्ध है, शुद्ध मेरा है।
verses.commentary: The repetition of "pure" is a meditative affirmation. The Self is inherently pure — untouched by the impurities of action and experience.
verses.wordMeaning: The repetition of "pure" is a meditative affirmation. The Self is inherently pure — untouched by the impurities of action and experience.

verses.sanskrit: योऽहं नेति योऽहं न जानाति योऽहं न वेद न मुमुक्षुः | स दुःखार्तिः स दुःखार्तिः स दुःखार्तिः स दुःखार्तिः ||
verses.transliteration: yo'haṃ neti yo'haṃ na jānāti yo'haṃ na veda na mumukṣuḥ | sa duḥkhārtiḥ sa duḥkhārtiḥ sa duḥkhārtiḥ sa duḥkhārtiḥ ||
verses.translation: He who does not know "I am not this," who does not know, who does not understand, who does not seek liberation — he is the cause of suffering, he is the cause of suffering, he is the cause of suffering, he is the cause of suffering.
verses.hindi: जो "मैं यह नहीं" नहीं जानता, जो नहीं जानता, जो नहीं समझता, जो मुक्ति नहीं चाहता — वह दुःख का कारण है, वह दुःख का कारण है, वह दुःख का कारण है, वह दुःख का कारण है।
verses.commentary: The repetition emphasises the suffering caused by ignorance. Not knowing the true Self is the root of all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The repetition emphasises the suffering caused by ignorance. Not knowing the true Self is the root of all suffering.

verses.sanskrit: योऽहं नेति योऽहं जानाति योऽहं वेद यो मुमुक्षुः | स शान्तोऽसौ स शान्तोऽसौ स शान्तोऽसौ स शान्तः ||
verses.transliteration: yo'haṃ neti yo'haṃ jānāti yo'haṃ veda yo mumukṣuḥ | sa śānto'sau sa śānto'sau sa śānto'sau sa śāntaḥ ||
verses.translation: He who knows "I am not this," who knows, who understands, who seeks liberation — he is peaceful, he is peaceful, he is peaceful, he is peaceful.
verses.hindi: जो "मैं यह नहीं" जानता है, जो जानता है, जो समझता है, जो मुक्ति चाहता है — वह शांत है, वह शांत है, वह शांत है, वह शांत है।
verses.commentary: The counterpart to verse 16. Knowledge of Self brings peace. The repetition of "peaceful" affirms the result of liberation.
verses.wordMeaning: The counterpart to verse 16. Knowledge of Self brings peace. The repetition of "peaceful" affirms the result of liberation.
